video_subject: The Great Attractor pulling the Milky Way galaxy
video_script: Right now, your entire body is moving through space at 1.3 million miles per hour, and you can't even feel it. Our entire galaxy, along with thousands of others, is being dragged toward a mysterious gravitational anomaly in deep space. Astronomers call it the Great Attractor. It lies 220 million light-years away, in a region hidden behind the thick stars and dust of our own Milky Way, known as the Zone of Avoidance. Its gravitational mass is equal to tens of thousands of galaxies combined. Even with our most powerful telescopes, we still cannot see what is inside it. Whatever is lurking in the dark is pulling everything toward itself, and we are getting closer every second.

video_subject: The Boötes Void: The scariest place in the universe
video_script: There is a terrifying region of deep space where almost nothing exists. It is called the Boötes Void, and it is 330 million light-years across. Based on the average density of the universe, this immense space should contain at least 10,000 galaxies. Instead, astronomers have found only about 60. To put that in perspective, if our Milky Way were placed in the center of the Boötes Void, we wouldn't have known other galaxies existed until the 1960s. The night sky would be completely black. Some physicists theorize it is just a natural cosmological fluctuation. Others wonder if something terrifying cleared it out.

video_subject: Rogue Planets: The giant dark wanderers drifting in interstellar space
video_script: Not every planet orbits a star. Deep in interstellar space, billions of frozen, homeless worlds drift through absolute darkness. These are rogue planets. Some were violently ejected from their solar systems during violent gravitational encounters with giant gas planets. Traveling alone through the freezing vacuum of space with no sunlight, their surfaces are frozen solid at hundreds of degrees below zero. Yet scientists believe some rogue planets might harbor deep sub-surface oceans, warmed by their own radioactive cores, where alien life could survive without ever seeing a sun. Billions of them are drifting out there right now.
